<issue>
dx fmt breaks indentation of commented-out RSX blocks (regression since v0.7.3)
Since v0.7.4 (commit b6793dc2b, PR #5257), `dx fmt` mangles the indentation of commented-out RSX blocks. Two variants:

**Variant 1: First line keeps indentation, rest gets dedented**

Idempotency test with this input fails:

```diff
 rsx! {
     div {
         h2 { "Title" }
         // div { class: "wrapper",
-        //     p { "A" }
-        //     p { "B" }
-        // }
+    //     p { "A" }
+    //     p { "B" }
+    // }
     }
 }
```

**Variant 2: Entire block gets dedented (nested rsx!)**

```diff
 rsx! {
     Component {
         field: rsx! {
             div {
                 h2 { "Title" }
-                // div { class: "wrapper",
-                //     // nested comment
-                //     p { "A" }
-                // }
+            // div { class: "wrapper",
+            //     // nested comment
+            //     p { "A" }
+            // }
             }
         },
     }
 }
```

Root cause is the rewritten comment-handling in `packages/autofmt/src/writer.rs` (PR #5257). Commented-out RSX blocks aren't covered by existing tests.

Happy to submit a PR with the test cases (and a fix) if that's helpful.

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

content.text:
I changed the trailing-comment handling in `packages/autofmt/src/writer.rs`. I haven't run it against the issue's two examples, and I didn't add tests for commented-out RSX blocks.

The trailing comments after an element's last child were written at the element's own indent level instead of the child level. They also went in after the closing brace's indentation had already been written. That is why the first comment line came out indented and the rest were pushed back to the element's level.

The fix removes that leftover indentation from the buffer. It then writes the comments one indent level deeper and restores the level before the closing brace.

`cargo test --offline -p dioxus-autofmt` passes. The helper only read the last 40 lines of output, so it saw the counts for three test files (48, 1 and 15 tests, all ok), not every file.

I only traced the first variant (the top-level `rsx!` case). I didn't trace the nested `rsx!` one separately. I expect the same code path to handle it, but I haven't confirmed that.
